dedupe_keys.name: annual 10 m maize maps for northeast china 2017 to 2024 alphaearth satellite embeddings

description: This dataset maps where maize was grown each year from 2017 to 2024 in Heilongjiang, Jilin and Liaoning, China's main grain-producing region, at 10 metre resolution. It was published on figshare in September 2026 by Xingguang Yan, Jingyi Le, Zhen Dong, Yuhuan Han and Lang Xia. Maps were produced on Google Earth Engine from AlphaEarth Foundations Satellite Embedding V1, with random forest classifiers trained separately for five agro-climate zones across 119 grids; training samples for 2017 to 2022 came from harmonising six existing crop products and were carried to 2023 and 2024 by cosine similarity of the 64-dimensional embeddings. Validation gave maize F1 scores of 0.915 to 0.936 against ground samples for 2017 to 2019, R squared of 0.78 to 0.90 against municipal statistical yearbooks and overall accuracies of 0.934 to 0.985 on test samples. The GeoTIFF files, about 2.8 GB with 1 for maize and 0 otherwise, are free to download under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: accuracy varies by zone and year, and later years rely on transferred samples. Simulation uses: crop location layers for exposure of food production to floods, drought and other hazards. Related records: the China 1 km maize and wheat yield data (data-china-maize-wheat-yield-water-productivity-1km) and GEOGLAM crop type masks (data-geoglam-best-available-crop-type-masks) are coarser crop layers.
